# 5. Interaction Flow Based on the above functional architecture and the integration model of Agent/Copilot, this chapter focuses on how to achieve end-to-end processing of the Core Network single-domain fault management through the interaction and cooperation of agents at the Resource layer and the Service layer. ## 5.1. AN L4 Core Network Fault Management Workflow [Figure: AN L4 Core Network Fault Management workflow] 1. Faults that require only manual review [1→2→3a→4a→5a→6a]: Over 90% of core network faults are automatically diagnosed by the Agent, which provides a repair plan that is automatically processed after NOC review. 2. Faults that require manual handling [1→2→3b→4b→5b→6b]: The Agent is unable to automatically diagnose or provide a repair plan, so the NOC uses Copilot to assist manually in handling the faults. Core network stability To ensure core network stability, e.g. in case of signaling storm, the core network management system requests MDAF (Management Data Analytics Function – 3GPP TS 28.104) to evaluate the potential risks and provide recommended actions. To achieve this, MDAF collects performance data and configuration data (such as node connections, signaling traffic, device status) from the core network. By using network digital twin, MDAF constructs a virtual image of the core network topology, real-time network traffic and core network NE / NF load conditions, so as to model signaling storms. MDAF analyzes the load capacity of NEs to identify bottlenecks. MDAF automatically generates optimization recommendations, including flow control parameter adjustment plans, and provides the core network management system with the potential impacts of signaling storm on the core network and the recommended flow control parameter adjustment plans. ## 5.3.
